speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your age and if you have any significant medical conditions or take any regular medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, have you experienced any involuntary muscle movements, rigidity, or excessive sweating recently? I need to assess for potential neuroleptic malignant syndrome or other drug-induced complications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of migraine is highly unlikely given the presence of generalized rigidity and profuse sweating, which strongly points toward Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase, CBC, CMP, Urinalysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated); Complete Blood Count: White Blood Cell Count 14,700/mm3 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis confirm Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
